thread:
sam: Quick q — I opened a tiny PR to bump oauth2-client in the ruby sampleapp to fix a TLS CI flake. @maria can you take a quick look? I'm seeing an intermittent 401 during local onboarding after a token rotate, trying to decide if we revert the bump or patch the sampleapp flow.

taylor: Repro steps I ran locally:
```
1) bundle exec ruby bin/sample_onboard.rb --env=local
2) complete login flow, then trigger token refresh (we call /refresh_token)
3) next request to /me returns 401 intermittently (~1/5 runs)
Logs:
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:33.456Z]  INFO -- : refresh response: {"access_token":"xxx","expires_in":3600} 
I, [2026-03-22T14:12:33.458Z] ERROR -- : 401 Unauthorized when calling /me (Authorization: Bearer xxx)
```

alex: saw same in yesterday's smoke run on macOS — CI was green but local dev hit it. Might be oauth2-client changing default header encoding or cookie storage.

maria: Hmm. Could be the gem bump changed how refresh token is returned (string vs JSON wrapper) or changed percent-encoding for scopes. Can you paste the exact response body from /refresh_token when it fails?

sam: Paste from failing run: `\{"access_token\":\"eyJ...\",\"token_type\":\"bearer\",\"expires_in\":3600\}` — looks normal. But after refresh the next request uses the token and sometimes it errors with 401. Minimal curl that repros intermittently: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJ...\" http://localhost:3000/me` returns 401 then 200 next try.

taylor: I added quick logging to token storage in sampleapp — sometimes the token saved to disk had a trailing newline when using the bumped gem's helper. If token file contains `\n` the Authorization header becomes `Bearer <token>\n` which some servers treat as invalid.

alex: oh interesting. Does the gem change how token.to_s or token.inspect behaves? That could introduce the newline in helpers.

maria: If that's the case, two short fixes: 1) sanitize token with `.strip` in sampleapp before storing/sending, 2) file an issue against oauth2-client and pin to previous version until resolved. Which do you prefer?

sam: I'll add a `.strip` guard in the sampleapp and a test that writes a token with newline to ensure we don't regress. I'll also add a note in the PR description about pinning vs bumping.

maria: Please add an integration spec that simulates token file with newline and assert header is correct. I'll do a quick review after you push the test. :+1:

sam: Cool — pushing a tiny follow-up in a minute. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: Note: CI job "ruby-sampleapp-smoke" re-run queued (jenkins/ruby-sampleapp-smoke #542).

taylor: Thanks — once the strip + test is in we should be safe to keep the gem bump. If oauth2-client wants to change behaviour in a patch, our test will catch it.

sam: Yep. Will update the PR and mark as ready for review. :thumbsup:
